title: Cognitive Dissonance Theory: Overview
text:
Cognitive dissonance describes the mental discomfort experienced by a person who holds two or more conflicting beliefs, ideas, or values, or when they act in a way that is inconsistent with their existing beliefs. The magnitude of this discomfort is proportional to the importance of the cognitions involved.

To reduce this uncomfortable tension, individuals are motivated to change one of the conflicting elements—either by changing a behavior, altering a belief, or adding new consonant cognitions (rationalizations) that justify the discrepancy. For example, smoking while knowing the health risks creates dissonance, which can be reduced by downplaying the danger or emphasizing personal freedom.

Understanding this mechanism provides insights into decision-making and attitude change, suggesting that individuals often modify their perceptions rather than facing direct behavioral or belief adjustments.
